problem: A plate of mass $M$ occupies the circle ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\le 3.$ Its mass density at any point is given by $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{4}{9\pi }M{x}^{2}.$ Find the radius of gyration of the plate about the $x$-axis.

activity_context.topic_title: Calculating the Radius of Gyration of a Plane Lamina

feedback.problem: A plate of mass $M$ occupies the part of the circle ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\le 4$ in the first quadrant. Its mass density at any point is given by $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{3}{8}Mx.$ Find the radius of gyration of the plate about the $y$-axis.
feedback.worked_solution:
For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{x}$ about the $x$-axis is given by
${R}_{x}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{x}$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{y}$ about the $y$-axis is given by
${R}_{y}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{y}$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{0}$ about the origin is given by
${R}_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

In polar coordinates, the region occupied by the plate is given by

$$
D={(r,\theta )\,:\,0\le r\le 2,\,\,0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2}}.
$$

The moment of inertia about the $y$-axis, in polar coordinates, is defined as

$$
{I}_{y}={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta ,
$$

where $\lambda (r,\theta )$ is the mass density function.

Also, the mass density in terms of polar coordinates is $\lambda (r,\theta )=\frac{3}{8}Mr\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .$
Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{3}{8}M{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{r}^{4}{cos}^{3}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{3}{8}M({\int }_{0}^{2}{r}^{4}\,\text{d}r)({\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{cos}^{3}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{3}{8}M\cdot \frac{1}{5}{r}^{5}{|}_{0}^{2}\cdot ({\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta (1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )\,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{12M}{5}{[\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -\frac{{sin}^{3}⁡\theta }{3}]}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{12M}{5}(1-\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =\frac{8M}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of gyration about the $x$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{y} & =\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{8M}{5}\cdot \frac{1}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{8}{5}}.\end{aligned}
$$
